solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: It’s ending for good, I state after session with old flame (13)

indicatorNotes.after: the I-and-state chunk comes after the session
indicatorNotes.with: the old flame is put together with the rest, in front

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
a term is a session, as at school or in court

annotation.surface: Someone declares a relationship over for good after one last session with an old flame.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a break-up speech, which hides that 'ending for good' is a noun phrase for the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Extermination is the complete, permanent ending of something.

entries.clue: King of the Blues, beset by rivals at table, goes out (4)

indicatorNotes.beset by: to be beset is to be surrounded, so the rivals go round the king

blocks.note: East and South, opponents at the bridge table

annotation.surface: A blues legend, hemmed in by card players, leaves the game.
annotation.walkthrough: In bridge, North–South play against East–West, so E and S sit on opposing sides. 'King of the Blues' is not a king at all but B.B. King's initials.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the tide, and any fortune or strength, is said to ebb as it recedes or goes out.

entries.clue: A far larger squat made into home for prominent metropolitan columnist (9,6)

indicatorNotes.made into: the letters are made into something new

annotation.surface: A squatted building is converted into a flat for a London newspaper columnist.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'columnist' is not a journalist but Nelson, standing on top of his column in London's Trafalgar Square; 'prominent' is literal, since the column is very tall.
annotation.definitionFit: Nelson's Column stands in Trafalgar Square, so the square is home to the metropolitan figure on a column.

entries.clue: Reshuffle back rank (9)

blocks.note: a rank or range is a row, as of hills

annotation.surface: A cabinet reshuffle demotes someone to the back ranks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rank' reads as status in a reshuffle, but here it means a row, as in a range of mountains.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to reshuffle a cabinet or a deck is to put its members in a new order.

entries.clue: Bay home to rent (5)

blocks.note: a house to let is for rent

annotation.surface: An advert for a house on a bay available to rent.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by size: a narrow arm of the sea running into the coast is a small bay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bay' could be a horse's colour or a tree, but here it is a stretch of coastline.

entries.clue: Soldier dropped in suitable American kit (9)

indicatorNotes.dropped in: the soldier is dropped, like a paratrooper, into the other word

annotation.surface: A paratrooper parachutes in wearing the proper American gear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropped in' is doubly apt: paratroopers are dropped from planes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: gear or equipment for a task, the kit you bring.

entries.clue: Victor’s wife concealed secret (5)

indicatorNotes.concealed: the wife is kept out of sight, so W disappears

blocks.note: W = wife, the abbreviation used in genealogies; it is removed

annotation.surface: The champion's wife kept something hidden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concealed' looks like the definition, but it is the instruction to hide the W; the definition is 'secret'.
annotation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts or feelings are private, secret ones.

entries.clue: Like all-seater stadium, nevertheless (15)

blocks.note: a ground with seats everywhere has no terraces, so split the answer into four words describing that
the straight sense: despite this, all the same

annotation.surface: A stadium went all-seater regardless of the fans.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer into four words, 'not with standing', and it describes a ground where every spectator has a seat.
annotation.definitionFit: The straight sense is a formal adverb meaning all the same; the cryptic sense splits it into 'not with standing', a ground where nobody stands.

entries.clue: Pro-establishment, old right party controlling House with support of Times (8)

indicatorNotes.controlling: the party holds the House within its grip
indicatorNotes.with support of: in a down clue, a support sits underneath, so X goes at the bottom

blocks.note: a to-do is a big fuss, a party
H = house, as on a map

annotation.surface: A political sketch: an old right-wing party runs the House, backed by The Times.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about Parliament and a newspaper, but 'House' is just H and 'Times' is the multiplication sign.
annotation.definitionFit: Orthodox views follow the accepted line, which is what supporting the establishment means.

entries.clue: Fight about commercial that’s boring (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes a thing (a tool that bores) rather than naming it

indicatorNotes.about: the fight goes round the commercial

annotation.surface: A grumble that a fight over a TV advert is tedious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' seems to mean dull, but it means making holes: a bradawl is a small tool for boring holes in wood.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the tool is named by what it does, boring small holes in wood.

entries.clue: Better keeping spades and joker (7)

indicatorNotes.keeping: the better keeps the spades inside

blocks.note: a punter is one who bets, a better

annotation.surface: A card-table remark: the one who is betting is holding spades and the joker.
annotation.walkthrough: The card words steer toward a pack of cards, but 'Better' is a person who bets and 'joker' is a wit.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a maker of puns is one kind of joker, or wit.

entries.clue: I’ll recount Scottish island returns with Conservative falling short (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is what a narrator would say of themselves

indicatorNotes.returns: the island comes back, written right to left
indicatorNotes.falling short: the Tory falls short of its last letter

blocks.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde; reversed to NARRA
a Tory is a Conservative; cut short to TOR

annotation.surface: Someone promises to tell the story of a Scottish island's returning Conservative who fell short.
annotation.definitionFit: A first-person definition: the storyteller is the one who says 'I'll recount'.
annotation.walkthrough: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde; the definition is a first-person line, the voice of the storyteller.

entries.clue: Austrian psychiatrist — note his ego (5)

blocks.note: re, the second note of the sol-fa scale
ich is German for 'I', the ego of a German speaker such as the psychiatrist

annotation.surface: A case note on an Austrian psychiatrist's own ego.
annotation.walkthrough: Ego is Latin for 'I'; 'his' asks for the word in the psychiatrist's own language, German ich.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by fact: Wilhelm Reich (1897–1957), the Austrian-born psychoanalyst known for orgone theory.

entries.clue: Sin City reversing direction, rejecting pleasures of flesh? (5)

indicatorNotes.reversing direction: one compass direction is swapped for its opposite, S for N

blocks.note: Las Vegas is nicknamed Sin City; its S becomes N

annotation.surface: Las Vegas turning its back on the pleasures of the flesh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pleasures of flesh' sounds sexual, which suits Sin City, but the definition means refusing to eat meat; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful definition: someone who refuses to eat any animal flesh, with 'pleasures of flesh' punning on the sexual sense.

entries.clue: Elves in legends ultimately transformed despicable character (8)

indicatorNotes.transformed: the letters are changed into a new form

annotation.surface: In the old legends the elves were turned into villains in the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: baseness or wickedness of nature, a despicable character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Legends ultimately' gives only the S; the elves provide the rest, so the anagram has eight letters.

entries.clue: Tears perhaps when children have to turn off TV? (9)

annotation.definition: when children have to turn off TV?

blocks.note: tears are liquid the eyes let fall; split the answer in two to see it

blocks.clueFragment: when children have to turn off TV?
blocks.note: the 9 pm cut-off in UK broadcasting, after which adult material may be shown

annotation.surface: A child in tears at bedtime when the television goes off.
annotation.walkthrough: Split as WATER SHED, it describes tears. In Britain the watershed is 9 pm, before which broadcasters must keep programmes suitable for children.
annotation.definitionFit: The TV sense is a British broadcasting term for the 9 pm line; the cryptic sense reads it as two words for tears.

entries.clue: Throw left instead of right? (5-4)

blocks.note: throw in the sense of disconcert, catch off balance
taking a step with the left when the right was needed; split the answer in two

annotation.surface: A thrower uses the left arm when they should have used the right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Throw' looks like hurling something, but it means to disconcert; split WRONG FOOT, it is literally the left one when the right was wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: To unsettle an opponent by catching them off balance; the second sense is the literal split, the incorrect foot.

entries.clue: Unusually chic broadcaster’s going outside and leaves for lunch? (9)

indicatorNotes.Unusually: the letters of 'chic' are arranged in an unusual way
indicatorNotes.going outside: the broadcaster goes round the outside of the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: A trendy broadcaster heads out and leaves for lunch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves for lunch' reads as someone departing to eat; the leaves are salad leaves, and the question mark flags that.
annotation.definitionFit: Radicchio is a red-leaved chicory eaten in salads.

entries.clue: Inclined to lift a clue? No sir, I’ll go for revision (9)

indicatorNotes.I’ll go: spoken by the clue as if by the letter I: 'I'll go' means the I departs from 'sir'
indicatorNotes.for revision: the remaining letters are up for revision, so rearranged

annotation.surface: A setter refuses to steal a clue, telling someone he'll go and revise it instead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lift' means steal, which makes 'lift a clue' an accusation of plagiarism in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Larcenous means given to theft, inclined to lift things.

entries.clue: Attempt to tackle addiction to amphetamine wraps (5)

blocks.note: Dex, short for Dexedrine, an amphetamine

annotation.surface: A programme to beat addiction to amphetamine, sold in wraps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like part of the definition, but it is the letters being wrapped; the definition ends at 'addiction'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a course of treatment to clear the body of drugs is an attempt to tackle addiction.

entries.clue: Extremists in Iraq accommodated by sanction over veil (5)

indicatorNotes.Extremists in: the letters at the two extremes of 'Iraq'
indicatorNotes.accommodated by: the IQ is housed inside the other word
indicatorNotes.over: the sanction is turned over, reading backwards

blocks.note: a ban is a sanction; turned over to NAB
the first and last letters of 'Iraq'

annotation.surface: A news line about Iraqi extremists and sanctions over the wearing of the veil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' sounds political, but it asks for the letters at the extremes of 'Iraq'.
annotation.definitionFit: A niqab is a veil covering the face, worn by some Muslim women.

entries.clue: Sign of rank, rotten egg served up — it’s unfinished (5)

indicatorNotes.served up: in a down clue, 'up' reads from the bottom, so the egg is turned upside down
indicatorNotes.unfinished: the egg loses its last letter

blocks.note: EGG with its last letter gone

annotation.surface: An officer's insignia reduced to a bad egg on a plate, half eaten.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: stripes, pips and insignia worn on a uniform are signs of rank.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'served up' means turned upside down, so the shortened egg reads upward.

entries.clue: Taking a gander and goose in van and skewering (8)

indicatorNotes.in van: the van is the front, so the goose leads

blocks.note: the first letter of 'goose', or G as its abbreviation

annotation.surface: A farmyard scene: a gander and a goose in a van, one of them being skewered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gander' tempts as the male goose beside 'goose', but 'taking a gander' is slang for having a look; 'in van' means in the vanguard, at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'take a gander' is informal for having a look, so a quick look fits.

entries.clue: Totters back, losing footing, after one followed by another one (5)

indicatorNotes.losing footing: in a down clue the foot is the last letter, which is dropped
indicatorNotes.after: the shortened back comes after the first 'one'
indicatorNotes.followed by: the whole is followed by the second 'one'

annotation.surface: Someone staggers backwards after one drink and then another.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Totters' reads as staggers, but here it is things that tot up, add: abacuses.
annotation.definitionFit: Abaci are counting frames, devices that tot up numbers.

entries.clue: Shock Brazil et al after making a comeback (4)

indicatorNotes.after making a comeback: the word comes back, reading upward

annotation.surface: A sports headline: Brazil and co. cause a shock with a comeback.
annotation.walkthrough: Brazil looks like the football team, but it is the Brazil nut.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to stun is to daze or astonish, as a shock does.

entries.clue: Leaders of seditious territorial army disgracefully don’t await orders (5,2)

indicatorNotes.Leaders of: take the first letter of each of the next three words
indicatorNotes.disgracefully: the letters of 'don't' behave badly, out of order

annotation.surface: A mutinous reserve unit shamefully ignores orders.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface says the soldiers disobey; the answer is the opposite, standing ready. The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
annotation.definitionFit: To stand to is to take up positions ready for action, awaiting orders.

entries.clue: I don’t believe article on America is true to begin with (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is what an atheist would say

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, the article goes on, after, America

annotation.surface: A sceptic doubts a newspaper article about America being true.
annotation.definitionFit: A first-person definition: the words a nonbeliever says about God.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a first-person line: a nonbeliever's own words. 'On' in an across clue means after, so the article follows America.

entries.clue: Instrument’s role for one of the Pacemakers? (8,5)

annotation.definition: Instrument’s role for one of the Pacemakers?

blocks.note: reads as asking what a band member plays
Gerry and the Pacemakers were a 1960s Liverpool band, but a medical pacemaker is also meant: a battery device that keeps the heart beating

annotation.surface: Which instrument does a member of the band Gerry and the Pacemakers play?
annotation.walkthrough: A heart pacemaker is an electric device working for an organ, the heart; a member of Gerry and the Pacemakers might play an electric organ.
annotation.definitionFit: The musical sense is a keyboard instrument; the medical sense reads it as the electric device's charge, the heart.
